statement: The first van der Corput / PET difference of the floor-Hardy Heisenberg lift re-enters the amplitude-product class. Write g(n) = (A(n), B(n), 0) with A = (3/2) v^{3/4}, B = v^{3/2}, v = floor(n^{3/2}). Heisenberg multiplication gives g(n)^{-1} g(n+h) = (ΔA, ΔB, -A ΔB). Mal'cev reduction to the fundamental domain [0,1)^3 yields the vertical chi_Δ = {-A ΔB - ΔA floor(ΔB)} = {-A(n+h) floor(ΔB) - A(n){ΔB}}. The first summand is integer dilation of {A(n+h)} (cheap A-axis). The second is the amplitude-product A{ΔB} with A ≍ n^{9/8} and A(n+2)-A(n) ~ (27/8) n^{1/8} >> 1 (GG species). Equivalently A{ΔB} is the vertical of a second Heisenberg lift of (A(n), ΔB(n,h), 0) — the same group law as J-tower-heisenberg-coordinate, not a degree drop to a published Hardy-nil orbit. The leftover of ΔB against (n+h)^{9/4}-n^{9/4} has size ≍ n^{3/4}, so the difference is not o(1)-close to a Hardy-in-n pair. This is a different identity from the v94 abelian difference {v(n+h)^{9/4}-v(n)^{9/4}}. Consequence: characteristic-factor / PET induction cannot keep the floor-removal correction as a coordinate through the first step. The rate-free conjecture is unharmed (Leibman on the horizontal remains the unbuilt composition). Not a K3 bound and not a Paper B edit.
